seed: Tilt, flip and push layers in depth from the canvas and the panel, at Next defaults with no flag changed. A title is typed over a recording at one second and picked: it wears the knob it always has and nothing new. Resting on the knob brings out the two arcs; the flat arc dragged sideways swings the title 40 degrees on Y, the pill under it says so, and the panel's 3D section reads 40. The Rotation Y diamond keys it, a second later the arc swings it on to 180, so the title flips over one second; the walk scrubs through the flip and photographs it. The depth arrow pushes it back. Then a rectangle is drawn, turned flat by the knob itself and moved, and its 3D rows stay at 0: plain 2D editing is unchanged.

steps.note: the title picked: its box, its handles and the turn knob above it, exactly as before. No arcs, no arrow, nothing new until the pointer rests on the knob

the title swung 40 degrees on Y: its right edge has gone away from you, so it is shorter than its left, and the outline, handles and knob sit on the turned card. The arcs are still out on the knob: green flat arc across it, red tall arc beside it, and the blue depth arrow off the middle
at two seconds the title has flipped all the way over and shows its back, mirrored. Two keys on Rotation Y, one at 1s and one at 2s
a quarter of the way through the flip: swung further than 40, the far edge shorter still
half way through the flip in time: near edge on
three quarters of the way: showing its back, nearly flat again
the title pushed back in depth by the blue arrow: smaller, toward the middle of the frame. Pivot depth has joined the 3D rows because the title is turned
a rectangle turned flat with the knob itself and then moved: it lies flat on the picture, its 3D rows read 0, and nothing about the turn or the move changed
